Thus, it helps in respiration."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the cause, symptoms and remedy of the disease where inner lining of the system gets inflamed in A.","marks":3,"answer":"The disease where inner lining of the system gets inflamed is called bronchitis. Its cause, symptoms and remedies are explained below:
Cause: The disease is caused by bacterial infection. Living in unhealthy conditions, inhaling dust, polluted air, smoking cigarettes and cold are some of the causes of bronchitis. Once attacked by bronchitis there is a possibility of recurring attack.
Symptoms:
i. Cough, chest pain and breathing distress.
ii. When coughing the patient feels severe chest pain.
iii. Fever and gradual weakness.
iv. Can not eat solid food.
v. Sputum is discharged with cough.
Remedy:
i. Stop smoking, drinking alcohol, use of tobacco.
ii. Follow treatment according to the physician's advice.
iii. Keep the patient in tolerable temperature and dry environment.
iv. Feed nutritious liquid and hot food, e.g. hot milk, soup etc.
v. Taking full rest."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Explain the function of B in gaseous exchange in the system.","marks":4,"answer":"B in the stem is lung. Its function in gaseous exchange in the system is explained below:
Gaseous exchange means the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide. It occurs in between the air and blood vessels of the lungs. Gaseous exchange occurs in two steps, the absorption of oxygen and the giving out or expelling of carbon dioxide.
Absorption of Oxygen: Gaseous exchange in the lungs occurs via diffusion, where \(\mathrm{O}_2\) combines with hemoglobin in red blood cells to form oxyhemoglobin. As \(\mathrm{O}_2\) is transported, it diffuses from plasma to lymph when the \(\mathrm{O}_2\) concentration in lymph is lower. It causes hemoglobin to release \(\mathrm{O}_2\) which then enters the plasma, lymph, and finally the cells. The diffusion of gases occurs due to gas pressure differences. Most oxygen binds with hemoglobin, forming oxyhemoglobin, which easily releases oxygen when needed.
\(\text{Haemoglobin} + \text{oxygen} \rightarrow \text{oxyhaemoglobin (unstable compound)}\)
\(\text{Oxyhaemoglobin} \rightarrow \text{free oxygen} + \text{haemoglobin}\)
Carbon dioxide transport: \(\text{CO}_2\), produced by food oxidation, diffuses through the cell membrane into the lymph and then into the blood plasma. It is primarily transported as bicarbonate (\(\text{NaHCO}_3\) in plasma and \(\text{KHCO}_3\) in red blood cells). In the lungs, \(\text{CO}_2\) is released from bicarbonate, diffuses into the alveoli, and is exhaled.
